title: Role Mask
definition: A protective identity structure built by cognition to navigate relational environments where emotional safety, validation, or attachment were uncertain or inconsistent.
summary: The Role Mask is a functional adaptation. It includes behaviors adopted to be accepted, beliefs repeated for belonging, roles taken on for survival, and emotions hidden for safety. It forms when the Real Self couldn't secure connection through authenticity alone.

content.title: What It Is
content.content: The Role Mask is the protective identity structure that forms when early environments require adaptation for survival. It includes: behaviors adopted to be accepted, beliefs repeated even if not our own, family or social roles taken on, gestures and speech patterns for belonging, emotions hidden or performed, and images projected outward. The Role Mask is not who we are — it's who we learned to be.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Maps It
content.content: TEG-Blue treats the Role Mask as a regulatory strategy organized around Pattern B (Protection). It forms through three conditions: emotionally unpredictable environments (requiring constant scanning), emotionally incongruent environments (requiring reality distortion), and emotional invalidation (requiring self-suppression). The mask that once protected connection eventually prevents it. Healing doesn't require destroying the mask but creating safety for the Real Self to re-emerge alongside it.

content.title: Research Basis
content.content: Integrates Winnicott's False Self, Jung's Persona, attachment strategies (Main), defensive structures (A. Freud), survival self (van der Kolk), and compensatory structures (Kohut). Six traditions independently identified a protective identity that forms in response to relational conditions. TEG-Blue synthesizes these through the Four-Mode Gradient.
